questions.prompt: How many valence electrons does an oxygen atom have?
Which molecule has a linear shape?
Explain why a molecule of water (H2O) has a bent molecular shape rather than a linear shape, despite having only two covalent bonds.
questions.answer: Water has a bent shape because the two lone pairs of electrons on the central oxygen atom exert a strong repulsive force that pushes the two hydrogen-oxygen covalent bonds closer together.
questions.rubric: 1 point: names the two lone pairs on the oxygen atom. 1 point: explains that their repulsion pushes the bonds together into a bent shape.
